author: hassansrainy
body:
## 📋 Problème identifié

Les images uploadées étaient servies dans leur taille et qualité originales. Une image de 2.14MB était chargée telle quelle, gaspillant 90% de bande passante. Pas de compression backend, pas de lazy loading frontend, pas d'attributs width/height causant du layout shift. Cause racine : ImageUploadController stockait les images sans traitement, et le frontend affichait sans optimisation.

## 🛠️ Solution implémentée

**Backend (8 pts)** : Installé Intervention Image avec support GD (libjpeg-dev, libfreetype6-dev ajoutés au Dockerfile). Implémenté optimisation automatique dans ImageUploadController : redimensionnement à max 1200px largeur, compression 80% qualité JPG, conversion de tous formats vers JPG. Test : 2.14MB PNG réduit à 64-228KB (89-97% de réduction). **Frontend (4 pts bonus)** : Ajouté loading="lazy" pour lazy loading natif, attributs width="600" height="400" pour éviter layout shift. Fichiers modifiés : backend/Dockerfile, backend/app/Http/Controllers/ImageUploadController.php, backend/composer.json, frontend/src/components/ImageUpload.jsx.

## ✅ Tests effectués

1. Upload 2.14MB PNG → Optimisé à 64KB (97% réduction) ✅
2. Image affichée avec lazy loading → Chargée uniquement quand visible ✅
3. Attributs width/height présents → Pas de layout shift ✅
4. Formats JPEG, PNG, GIF supportés → Tous convertis en JPG ✅
5. Images redimensionnées à max 1200px largeur ✅

## 💭 Questions à considérer

**Backend** : Package PHP Intervention Image 2.7.2 utilisé (compatible PHP 7.4). Optimisation lors de l'upload pour éviter de stocker les originaux lourds. Dimensions 1200px max car suffisant pour affichage web. Images existantes non migrées (scope du ticket limité aux nouvelles). **Frontend** : Lazy loading via attribut HTML natif loading="lazy". Attributs width/height réservent l'espace avant chargement, évitant le décalage de layout. **Full-stack** : Mesure DevTools Network, gain de 89-97% sur le poids. Impact majeur sur performance mobile et connexions lentes.

author: copilot
body:
Builds the core intelligence layer for the Legal Counsel system: expert profile generation for 29 legal specialties and consensus-based fact verification using 3 AI models.

## Implementation

**`server/legalCounselExpertSystem.ts`** - Generates law-specific expert personas
- 29 unique profiles: specialty, 25-32 years experience, tone (empathetic/analytical/authoritative/balanced), focus areas
- Meticulousness levels: 9 (high complexity: tax, IP, bankruptcy, constitutional, immigration, estate), 7 (medium: business, employment, real estate, healthcare, environmental, administrative), 6 (standard: others)
- System prompts with accuracy requirements, source attribution mandates, jurisdiction-specific guidance, ethical boundaries
- Response structure varies by meticulousness: 8+ = 4-6 paragraphs, 6+ = 2-3 paragraphs, <6 = 1-2 paragraphs

**`server/factCheckingEngine.ts`** - Multi-model verification with consensus logic
- Parallel execution across Gemini, Groq, Claude (Promise.all)
- Consensus: 2/3+ agreement (verified ≥ 2) OR unanimous disagreement (verified = 0)
- Verification requires: consensus AND confidence ≥ 0.7
- Claim extraction patterns: statutes (`Cal. Penal Code § 484`), case law (`Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436`), legal principles (sentences starting with "Under", "According to", etc.)
- Citation deduplication by statute name (case-insensitive)
- Conservative error handling: unverified on failure, temperature 0.1, JSON mode

## Example Usage

```typescript
// Expert configuration
const config = getExpertSystemConfig('criminal-law', 'CA');
// Returns: Criminal Defense & Prosecution, 25-32 years, authoritative tone

// Fact verification
const result = await checkFact({
  claim: "California Penal Code § 484 covers theft offenses",
  context: { lawType: 'criminal-law', state: 'CA' }
});
// Returns: verified status, 3 model results, consensus boolean, confidence 0-1, merged citations

// Claim extraction
const claims = extractClaimsFromResponse("Under California Penal Code § 484...");
// Returns: ["California Penal Code § 484", ...]
```

## Integration

Pure backend logic with zero dependencies on API routes, database, or UI. Imports only from existing `aiProvider.ts` and `shared/legalCounselTypes.ts`. No breaking changes - completely additive.

Ready for Phase 1A-2 (API routes and database integration).

body:
When using my own button on an uncontrolled `Menu` component, clicking the button once while the menu was open was closing then re-opening the menu. (Similar to https://github.com/szhsin/react-menu/issues/838)

The issue was that my own button was accepting the `onClick` and `onKeyDown` props, as documented here: https://szhsin.github.io/react-menu#customised-btn

However, `onMouseDown` must also be passed to the button as found here: https://github.com/szhsin/react-menu/blob/dd5a8d9088c5115234573bd5dc1ddf0df564d81e/src/components/Menu.js#L67 and https://github.com/szhsin/react-menu/blob/dd5a8d9088c5115234573bd5dc1ddf0df564d81e/src/hooks/useClick.js#L10

This PR updates the documentation to reflect that.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a mobile-optimized slideshow gallery option for the stacked gallery view type. When enabled, users will see the stacked gallery on desktop and an OwlCarousel slideshow on mobile devices.

## Features

- **Customizer Option**: New "Use Slideshow on Mobile" toggle under WooCommerce > Single Product > Gallery settings (only visible when Stacked Gallery is selected)
- **OwlCarousel 2.3.4**: Responsive slider with touch/swipe support, arrow navigation, and thumbnail sync
- **Fancybox 5.0**: Lightbox/zoom functionality (different from Blocksy's built-in PhotoSwipe)
- **Responsive Design**: Automatically switches between stacked (desktop) and slideshow (mobile) at 767px breakpoint

## Technical Details

### New Files
- `assets/vendor/owlcarousel/` - OwlCarousel library files (local, not CDN)
- `assets/vendor/fancybox/` - Fancybox library files (local, not CDN)
- `assets/js/mobile-gallery.js` - Custom JS for slider initialization and sync
- `assets/css/slideshow-on-mobile.css` - Styling for gallery, arrows, thumbnails, zoom button
- `includes/customization/slideshow-on-mobile.php` - Main implementation class

### Modified Files
- `functions.php` - Added include for the new customization file

### How It Works
1. Adds `ct-stacked-with-mobile-slideshow` class to gallery container when enabled
2. Renders both stacked gallery and OwlCarousel slideshow in DOM
3. CSS toggles visibility based on viewport width (767px breakpoint)
4. JavaScript initializes OwlCarousel with thumbnail sync and Fancybox for lightbox

## Testing

1. Go to Customizer > WooCommerce > Single Product > Gallery
2. Select "Stacked Gallery" as the gallery type
3. Enable "Use Slideshow on Mobile" option
4. View a product page on mobile device or resize browser to ≤767px
5. Verify:
   - Desktop: Stacked gallery displays
   - Mobile: OwlCarousel slideshow displays with arrows, thumbnails, and zoom
